title: Crop diversification promotes soil microbial carbon turnover.
authors: Feng Wenhao; Gunina Anna; Peixoto Leanne; Shi Lingling; Mganga Kevin Z et al.
abstract: Agricultural diversification alters plant residue chemistry and rhizodeposition, with legacy effects on soil organic matter (SOM) cycling. The priming effect (PE) and necromass formation are key processes of SOM dynamics, yet how diversification affects these processes, and SOM persistence remains poorly understood. Using 13C-labelled glucose in a 150-day incubation of soils (0-15 cm) from two contrasting diversification trials (43 and 8 years), we found that diversification increased SOM priming by 153-174% and retention of glucose-derived 13C in microbial necromass by 227-289%. Diversified soils also had more bioavailable C, dissolved organic C, and neutral sugars, stronger stoichiometric nutrient limitation (103% higher C:P imbalance and 15% lower vector angle), and higher microbial activity and N- and P-acquiring enzyme activities. Microbial C use efficiency increased by 65%, while replacing the native microbial community of diversified soils with that of conventional soils reduced CUE by 9% and 45% at the 43- and 8-year sites, respectively. Community-level analyses further linked greater retention of glucose-derived 13C in microbial necromass to putative Discosea and Bacillota co-occurrence patterns. Metagenomic profiling revealed 18-125% higher relative abundances of CAZyme genes involved in degrading plant- and microbial-derived compounds, alongside a modest (~4%) increase in Y-associated functional potential at both sites. Although priming-induced native-C losses exceeded the amount of glucose-derived 13C retained in microbial necromass, the ratio of necromass C retention to priming-induced C loss was 28% higher under diversification than under conventional cropping over the 150-day incubation. Crop diversification thus reshapes microbial C cycling, coupling enhanced native SOM mineralization with greater retention of added C in microbial necromass, making the net effect on SOC dependent on sustained C inputs.
